abbreviations.expansion: abelian groups, or abelian sheaves in the displayed Ab(Y) context

notes: [S013.N1] This wholly handwritten continuation raises relative cohomology and gives case a), a displayed expression with a cancelled Gamma index, and the lower annotation résol. inj. It has no new title, date, salutation, signature, author page number or total. The separate pencil archive number is 12. The pen hand remains unnamed. H’s explicitly editorial page-order paragraph is not source ink and was not used to reorder the supplied scans.

[S013.N2] The question is whether relative cohomology can be defined functorially in an abelian sheaf, or a complex of such sheaves, on Y, from the derived category of the written Ab(Y) to that of Ab. The geometric interpretation in terms of n-champs de Picard, with n “grand”, is said to suggest existence: “suggère que ça doit exister”. The author says he sees a construction “à la main” only in two extreme cases; only a) occurs here. These are a question, a suggestion and a stated limitation, not a theorem proved in this run.

[S013.N3] Case a) calls the q/g morphism “(-1)-acyclique” and states an injectivity condition. The actual short relation after F is a dash, without a visible arrowhead. For a limited mathematical check, interpret the injectivity statement as the unit map F→g_*g^*F being monic, and take an abelian sheaf F with a bounded-below injective resolution I of g^*F. Left exactness makes F[0]→g_*I degreewise monic. Its cokernel Q fits 0→F[0]→g_*I→Q→0, hence Q[-1]→F→g_*I→Q. Exactness of g^* implies that its right adjoint g_* preserves injectives, so g_*I represents Rg_*g^*F; applying RΓ_Y gives the corresponding relative-sections triangle. This supports the written shift [-1] in that restricted sheaf case. It does not prove a canonical cone functor on bare triangulated categories, extend the argument to arbitrary unbounded complexes, or replace the source’s dash by an arrow. The calculation uses the abstract name g; the final source transcription has q/g after the cross-page ink review.

[S013.N4] The NB gives a slice-to-topos example under an epimorphism condition and a B-object reference “plus haut”. These assertions are carried as background without a separate proof. The object letter remains p/P, the connective si/où, and the two B subscripts c/e and c/G; no expected terminal-object or classifying-topos notation was used to decide them. The recurring morphism is q/g at first occurrence. The adjective remains évident/évidente, preserving the visible ending rather than grammar.

[S013.N5] The final formula retains its cancelled Y/X index, the doubtful [/( opener, four written round closes after F before [-1], and the brace through the first close. The resolution glyph resolves to e on an interior return, not H’s C. The abbreviation label has both stops. The formula’s delimiter mismatch is preserved. Small letters and the brace prompted close visual inspection, not a reconstruction from the mathematical expectation.

[S013.N6] Main’s crops of the two category names show a narrow interior return parallel to A’s outer left leg. A doubled/plain A doubt is therefore recorded at first occurrence, with a plain b; all three readers had treated the A as ordinary. This is a graphic uncertainty rather than a macro-only mathit/Mathrm preference. A separate high point beside the opening quote and two lower detached black points are preserved with no-textual-character alternatives. These alternatives acknowledge physical marks without assigning a textual function.

[S013.N7] All three complete independent readings and their difference lists were compared. Main inspected thirteen retained B crops, three retained A crops, and nine new crops for half-settled differences: twenty-five distinct crops. No source whole or half was viewed by main. Fourteen loci remain unresolved. The brief already covered isolated marks, but ordinary-font comparison rules needed clarification: differences between mathit and mathrm alone are not substantive, while an extra parallel stroke must be examined before calling the alphabet ordinary. The next brief makes that distinction explicit.

[S013.N8] The later cross-page notation review reused B/c01, B/c07, B/c08 and A/c14, without a new crop or whole/half view. Compared with scan014’s same letter family, the straight descending stems favour q, while the short terminal hooks keep g possible. Candidate order is now q/g on both pages; earlier independent readings and the pre-review decision are preserved. The e in this page’s resolution remains distinct from scan014’s C because the interior return is visible here. This review is a visual adjudication, not a new mathematical check.

check_events.outcome: Interpretation used only for this check: the written injectivity condition is treated as the unit-map assumption, while the transcription preserves the actual dash after F. Limited to an abelian sheaf F and a bounded-below injective resolution I of g^*F: if the unit F→g_*g^*F is monic, its composite F[0]→g_*I is degreewise monic. In degree 0, left exactness of g_* preserves g^*F→I^0; in other degrees F[0] is zero. With Q the degreewise cokernel, 0→F[0]→g_*I→Q→0 is a short exact sequence of complexes and yields Q[-1]→F→g_*I→Q. Since exact g^* is left adjoint to g_*, g_* preserves injectives, so g_*I represents Rg_*g^*F. Applying RΓ_Y gives the corresponding shifted-cone relative-sections triangle. This verifies the sign of [-1] and the construction for this restricted sheaf case; it does not prove a canonical cone functor on bare triangulated categories, the unbounded-complex extension, or the asserted BG example.
